title: The Loudest Sound Ever Recorded In History! 🌋 #shorts #science #history
description: In 1883, the Krakatoa volcanic eruption created a sound so loud it circled the Earth 4 times. #shorts #volcano #geology #earthfacts
text: In 1883, the Earth produced a sound so insanely loud it ruptured eardrums forty miles away and circled the entire globe four times. When the Krakatoa volcano exploded, the acoustic shockwave peaked at over three hundred and ten decibels. The blast was heard clearly three thousand miles away, shattered barometers across Europe, and registered on pressure gauges worldwide for days. title: You Are Living 80 Milliseconds In The Past 🧠 #shorts #brain #psychology
description: Your brain buffers reality, meaning you have never experienced the present moment in real time. #shorts #neuroscience #mindblown #facts
text: You have never seen the present moment in your entire life. You are living eighty milliseconds in the past. It takes time for light entering your eyes to convert into electrical signals, travel down the optic nerve, and reach your visual cortex. To prevent a disjointed picture of reality, your brain buffers sensory information, meaning everything you perceive right now actually happened eighty milliseconds ago. title: On This Planet, A Day Is Longer Than A Year! 🪐 #shorts #space #astronomy
description: Venus spins so slowly that its day outlasts its entire orbit around the Sun. #shorts #spacefacts #universe #solarsystem
text: Did you know that on Venus, a single day lasts longer than an entire Venusian year? Venus spins on its axis so extraordinarily slowly that it takes two hundred and forty-three Earth days to complete just one full rotation. However, it takes only two hundred and twenty-five Earth days to orbit the Sun. Even crazier, Venus rotates backwards, meaning the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east. title: The Boiling River That Cooks Animals Alive 🌊 #shorts #earth #nature
description: Deep in the Amazon rainforest, the Mayantuyacu river reaches boiling temperatures without any volcanoes. #shorts #amazon #river #mystery
text: Hidden deep in the Peruvian Amazon is a four-mile river that is literally boiling hot enough to cook animals alive. The Mayantuyacu river reaches temperatures of nearly two hundred degrees Fahrenheit. Unlike most thermal hot springs, this river has no volcanoes nearby. Instead, geothermal energy from deep faults within the Earth superheats underground water, blasting it up through the riverbed at fatal boiling temperatures. title: Your Phone Charger Is Smarter Than Apollo 11 🚀 #shorts #technology #space
description: The computer that landed humanity on the Moon had less memory than a modern USB-C charging block. #shorts #techfacts #nasa #moonlanding
text: The navigation computer that landed humans on the Moon had less computing power than a modern USB-C phone charger. In 1969, the Apollo Guidance Computer guided astronauts to the lunar surface using just four kilobytes of RAM. Today, a standard fast-charging USB-C brick contains a microchip with over fifty times more memory and processing speed just to negotiate electrical wattage with your phone. title: Clouds Weigh Over 1 Million Pounds! ☁️ #shorts #science #weather
description: That fluffy white cloud in the sky actually weighs more than 100 adult elephants. #shorts #physics #clouds #weatherfacts
text: That fluffy white cloud floating peacefully in the sky weighs over one million pounds. A typical cumulus cloud is about one kilometer across and holds a volume of one billion cubic meters. Because water droplets have mass, all that suspended moisture equals roughly five hundred thousand kilograms of water, the exact weight of one hundred adult elephants.
